questions.text:
निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(i) अफगानिस्तान पर सोवियत संघ का आक्रमण
(ii) रूस की क्रांति
(iii) ताजिकिस्तान में गृहयुद्ध का अंत
(iv) बर्लिन की दीवार का गिरना
सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in the chronological order :
(i) Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
(ii) Russian Revolution
(iii) End of Civil War in Tajikistan
(iv) Fall of the Berlin Wall
Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B): (ii), (i), (iv), (iii). The Russian Revolution occurred in 1917. The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan took place in 1979. The Berlin Wall fell in 1989. The Civil War in Tajikistan ended in 1997. Thus, the correct chronological order is Russian Revolution → Soviet invasion of Afghanistan → Fall of the Berlin Wall → End of Civil War in Tajikistan.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है: (ii), (i), (iv), (iii)। रूस की क्रांति 1917 में हुई। अफगानिस्तान पर सोवियत संघ का आक्रमण 1979 में हुआ। बर्लिन की दीवार 1989 में गिरी। ताजिकिस्तान में गृहयुद्ध का अंत 1997 में हुआ।
questions.topic: Chronology of Cold War Era Events

questions.text: रूस के कौन-से दो गणराज्यों में हिंसक अलगाववादी आंदोलन हुए थे ?
questions.text_english: Which two republics of Russia have had violent secessionist movements ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): Chechnya and Dagestan. Both Chechnya and Dagestan are republics within the Russian Federation that witnessed violent secessionist movements. Chechnya fought two major wars against Russia seeking independence. Dagestan also experienced armed insurgency linked to Chechen separatists. Azerbaijan and Croatia are independent countries, not republics of Russia, and Uzbekistan is a Central Asian nation — making options A, B, and D incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है: चेचन्या और दागिस्तान। ये दोनों रूस के गणराज्य हैं जहाँ हिंसक अलगाववादी आंदोलन हुए। अज़रबैजान और क्रोएशिया स्वतंत्र देश हैं, रूस के गणराज्य नहीं।
questions.topic: Disintegration of Soviet Union and its aftermath

questions.text: शक्ति संतुलन में देशों से निम्नलिखित में से किसकी अपेक्षा होती है ?
questions.text_english: Balance of power requires countries to __________.

options.A: विशेष प्रकार के हथियार त्यागने की
options.B: हथियारों को प्राप्त और विकसित करने की प्रक्रिया को नियमित करने की
options.C: सैन्य हमले से रक्षा के लिए अपनी कार्रवाइयों में सहयोग बनाने की
options.D: अन्य देशों के साथ अनुकूल संतुलन बनाने की

options_english.A: give up certain kinds of weapons
options_english.B: regulate acquisition and development of weapons
options_english.C: coordinate their actions to defend against military attack
options_english.D: maintain a favourable balance with other countries

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): maintain a favourable balance with other countries. The concept of balance of power in international relations requires that no single state should be allowed to become so powerful that it can dominate all others. Countries therefore seek to maintain a favourable equilibrium with other nations through alliances, arms build-up, or diplomatic arrangements. Options A and B relate to arms control, and option C relates to collective security — both are distinct concepts from balance of power.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। शक्ति संतुलन में देशों से अपेक्षा होती है कि वे अन्य देशों के साथ अनुकूल संतुलन बनाए रखें ताकि कोई एक राष्ट्र इतना शक्तिशाली न हो जाए कि वह सभी पर हावी हो सके।

questions.text: वे लोग जो अपना घर-बाग छोड़ जाते हैं लेकिन राष्ट्रीय सीमाओं के भीतर ही रहते हैं ?
questions.text_english: People who flee their homes but remain within national borders are called ____________.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): internally displaced people. When individuals or communities are forced to flee their homes due to conflict, violence, or disasters but do not cross an international border, they are termed internally displaced persons (IDPs). Refugees, by contrast, cross international boundaries. Migrants move voluntarily for economic or other reasons. Fugitives are those fleeing from law. Indigenous people refers to native inhabitants of a region — none of these match the definition in the question.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। जो लोग अपना घर छोड़ देते हैं लेकिन राष्ट्रीय सीमाओं के भीतर रहते हैं, उन्हें आंतरिक रूप से विस्थापित जन (IDP) कहा जाता है।

questions.text:
सूची I का सूची II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
सूची I — सूची II
1. क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल — (i) विकासात्मक नियमाचार की सूची
2. बिजली अधिनियम 2003, भारत — (ii) पारिस्थितिक तंत्र के प्रति उत्तरदायित्व के साथ आर्थिक वृद्धि
3. एजेंडा 21 — (iii) ग्रीनहाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन को कम करने का उद्देश्य
4. सतत पोषणीय विकास — (iv) नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा के प्रयोग को विकल्प
questions.text_english:
Match List I with List II and choose the correct option :
List I — List II
1. Kyoto Protocol — (i) List of developmental practices
2. Electricity Act of 2003, India — (ii) Economic growth with ecological responsibility
3. Agenda 21 — (iii) Aims to cut greenhouse gas emissions
4. Sustainable Development — (iv) Encourages use of renewable energy
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): 1-(iii), 2-(iv), 3-(i), 4-(ii). The Kyoto Protocol (1997) aims specifically to cut greenhouse gas emissions (iii). India's Electricity Act of 2003 encourages use of renewable energy sources (iv). Agenda 21 is a comprehensive action plan listing developmental practices for sustainable development adopted at the Rio Earth Summit (i). Sustainable Development itself is defined as economic growth carried out with ecological responsibility (ii).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल का उद्देश्य ग्रीनहाउस गैसों का उत्सर्जन कम करना है। भारत का बिजली अधिनियम 2003 नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा को बढ़ावा देता है। एजेंडा 21 विकासात्मक नियमाचार की सूची है। सतत विकास का अर्थ पारिस्थितिक उत्तरदायित्व के साथ आर्थिक वृद्धि है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : वैश्विक रणनीति में तेल आज भी सबसे महत्त्वपूर्ण संसाधन बना हुआ है।
कारण (R) : तेल से जुड़ी अपार संपदा राजनीतिक संघर्षों को जन्म देती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Oil continues to be the most important resource in global strategy.
Reason (R) : The immense wealth associated with oil generates political struggles.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Oil remains the most critical resource in global strategic calculations because it powers industries, militaries, and economies. The massive wealth generated from oil revenues has repeatedly fuelled political conflicts — such as those in the Middle East — and caused great power competition. Therefore, the immense wealth associated with oil is indeed the reason why it continues to dominate global strategy.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। तेल की अपार संपदा राजनीतिक संघर्षों को जन्म देती है, इसीलिए वैश्विक रणनीति में तेल सबसे महत्त्वपूर्ण संसाधन बना हुआ है।

questions.text: 1952 में कौन-सी राजनीतिक पार्टी जम्मू और कश्मीर में सत्ता में आई थी ?
questions.text_english: Which political party came to power in Jammu and Kashmir in 1952 ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): National Conference. In 1952, Jammu and Kashmir held its first elections after accession to India. Sheikh Abdullah's National Conference came to power and formed the government. The Indian National Congress did not contest these elections in J&K separately. Kashmir National Congress never existed as a party, and the Communist Party of India had no significant presence in J&K at that time.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस है। 1952 में जम्मू-कश्मीर में हुए पहले चुनावों में शेख अब्दुल्ला के नेतृत्व में नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस सत्ता में आई।

questions.text: भारत का निर्वाचन आयोग किस वर्ष गठित किया गया था ?
questions.text_english: In which year was the Election Commission of India set up ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B): 1950. The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950, the day before India became a Republic. It was set up under Article 324 of the Constitution to supervise, direct, and control the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures. Sukumar Sen was appointed as the first Chief Election Commissioner.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 1950 है। भारत का निर्वाचन आयोग 25 जनवरी 1950 को संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 के तहत स्थापित किया गया था। सुकुमार सेन इसके पहले मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त थे।

questions.text: दलाई लामा ने निम्नलिखित में से किस देश में राजनीतिक शरण प्राप्त की थी ?
questions.text_english: In which of the following countries did Dalai Lama obtain political asylum ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): India. In 1959, after the Chinese military suppression of the Tibetan uprising, the Dalai Lama fled Tibet and was granted political asylum in India. He established the Tibetan government-in-exile in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh, which is often called 'Little Lhasa'. This caused a major strain in India-China relations. Nepal, Bhutan, and Myanmar did not grant him political asylum.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) भारत है। 1959 में चीन द्वारा तिब्बत में विद्रोह को दबाने के बाद दलाई लामा ने भारत में शरण ली और धर्मशाला में तिब्बत की निर्वासित सरकार स्थापित की।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : 1979 में, ऑल असम स्टूडेंट्स यूनियन (AASU) ने बाहरी लोगों के विरुद्ध आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किया।
कारण (R) : आंदोलन अवैध अप्रवासियों तथा गलत मतदाता सूचियों के विरुद्ध था।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In 1979, All Assam Students Union (AASU) led the anti-foreigner movement.
Reason (R) : The movement was against illegal migrations and against faulty electoral rolls.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The AASU launched the Assam Agitation in 1979 specifically because it was concerned about illegal migrants — primarily from Bangladesh — who had settled in Assam and were included in voter rolls. The movement demanded that all illegal foreigners be identified and expelled. Since the Reason directly explains the cause behind the anti-foreigner agitation, option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। AASU ने 1979 में असम आंदोलन इसलिए शुरू किया क्योंकि अवैध अप्रवासी मतदाता सूचियों में शामिल हो गए थे।

questions.text: गुटनिरपेक्ष आंदोलन (NAM) का प्रथम शिखर सम्मेलन कहाँ आयोजित किया गया था ?
questions.text_english: The first summit of NAM was held in :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B): Belgrade. The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was held in Belgrade, Yugoslavia, in September 1961. It was attended by 25 founding member states. The summit was co-hosted by Yugoslav President Tito, along with leaders Jawaharlal Nehru of India, Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, Sukarno of Indonesia, and Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana. Cairo hosted the second NAM summit in 1964.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) बेलग्रेड है। गुटनिरपेक्ष आंदोलन का पहला शिखर सम्मेलन सितंबर 1961 में बेलग्रेड, यूगोस्लाविया में आयोजित हुआ था।

questions.text: खासी हिल्स भारत के किस राज्य में स्थित हैं ?
questions.text_english: In which state of India are the Khasi Hills located ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): Meghalaya. The Khasi Hills are a hilly region located in the state of Meghalaya in northeastern India. The Khasi people are an indigenous community inhabiting this region. The state of Meghalaya was carved out of Assam in 1972. Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are other northeastern states but do not contain the Khasi Hills.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) मेघालय है। खासी हिल्स मेघालय राज्य में स्थित हैं। खासी लोग इस क्षेत्र के मूल निवासी हैं।

questions.text: पूर्वी पाकिस्तान में 1970 के चुनावों में, किस राजनीतिक पार्टी ने किस नेता के नेतृत्व में सभी सीटों पर विजय प्राप्त की थी ?
questions.text_english: Which political party won all the seats in the 1970 elections in East Pakistan and under whose leadership ?

key_points: Awami League won all the seats in East Pakistan in the 1970 elections.
The elections were held under the leadership of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.
key_points_hindi: अवामी लीग ने 1970 के चुनावों में पूर्वी पाकिस्तान की सभी सीटें जीतीं।
ये चुनाव शेख मुजीबुर रहमान के नेतृत्व में लड़े गए।

questions.solution: In the 1970 general elections held in Pakistan, the Awami League, led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, won an overwhelming majority of seats in East Pakistan. The Awami League secured enough seats to form a government at the national level, but military ruler Yahya Khan and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto of West Pakistan refused to transfer power. This refusal to honour the election results led directly to the political crisis that culminated in the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971.
questions.solution_hindi: 1970 के पाकिस्तान आम चुनावों में शेख मुजीबुर रहमान के नेतृत्व में अवामी लीग ने पूर्वी पाकिस्तान में सभी सीटों पर भारी जीत दर्ज की। अवामी लीग राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर सरकार बनाने में सक्षम थी, लेकिन याह्या खान और भुट्टो ने सत्ता हस्तांतरण से मना कर दिया, जिससे 1971 का युद्ध हुआ।

questions.text: वैश्विक सुरक्षा का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of Global Security.

key_points: Global security refers to measures taken by nations and international organisations to ensure mutual safety from threats that transcend national boundaries.
It includes threats like terrorism, climate change, nuclear proliferation, pandemics, and economic crises that no single nation can address alone.
key_points_hindi: वैश्विक सुरक्षा उन उपायों को संदर्भित करती है जो राष्ट्र और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठन राष्ट्रीय सीमाओं से परे खतरों से निपटने के लिए करते हैं।
इसमें आतंकवाद, जलवायु परिवर्तन, परमाणु प्रसार, महामारी जैसे खतरे शामिल हैं।

questions.solution: Global security refers to the collective efforts of nations and international organisations to address threats that are transnational in nature and cannot be managed by any single country acting alone. These threats include international terrorism, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, climate change, global pandemics, and economic instability. Global security thus goes beyond traditional military defence and emphasises cooperation among nations through institutions like the United Nations to tackle shared vulnerabilities affecting all of humanity.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्विक सुरक्षा का अर्थ है राष्ट्रों और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठनों के सामूहिक प्रयास जो ऐसे खतरों से निपटते हैं जो किसी एक देश की सीमाओं से परे हों। इसमें अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आतंकवाद, परमाणु अप्रसार, जलवायु परिवर्तन, वैश्विक महामारी और आर्थिक अस्थिरता जैसे मुद्दे शामिल हैं।

questions.text: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना की कोई दो विशेषताएँ उजागर कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two features of the First Five Year Plan.

key_points: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) focused primarily on agriculture and irrigation to solve the food crisis inherited from Partition.
It was based on the Harrod-Domar model and aimed at modest economic targets, achieving a growth rate of 3.6% against the target of 2.1%.

questions.text: 1952 में भारत के आम चुनाव पूरे विश्व में लोकतंत्र के इतिहास के लिए मील का एक पत्थर बन गए ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did the general elections of 1952 become a landmark in the history of democracy all over the world ? Explain.

key_points: The 1952 elections were the first general elections held in independent India based on the principle of universal adult franchise.
They were the largest democratic exercise ever held in the world at that time, with nearly 17 crore eligible voters, demonstrating that democracy could function in a large, poor, and diverse country.
key_points_hindi: 1952 के चुनाव स्वतंत्र भारत में सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार के आधार पर आयोजित पहले आम चुनाव थे।
यह उस समय दुनिया में हुआ सबसे बड़ा लोकतांत्रिक चुनाव था।

questions.solution: The general elections of 1952 became a landmark in the history of world democracy for two major reasons. First, they were the first elections in independent India conducted on the basis of universal adult franchise, giving every citizen above 21 years the right to vote regardless of caste, class, or gender. Second, with nearly 17 crore eligible voters across a vast, poor, and largely illiterate country, they were the largest democratic exercise in human history at that time, proving that democracy was viable even in complex and diverse societies.
questions.solution_hindi: 1952 के भारत के आम चुनाव विश्व लोकतंत्र के इतिहास में मील का पत्थर इसलिए बने क्योंकि ये सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार के आधार पर आयोजित पहले चुनाव थे और लगभग 17 करोड़ मतदाताओं के साथ उस समय का सबसे बड़ा लोकतांत्रिक अभ्यास था।

questions.text: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानदंडों और संस्थाओं को मजबूती प्रदान करने से किस प्रकार भारत ने अपने सुरक्षा हितों की रक्षा की है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How has the strengthening of international norms and international institutions helped India protect its security interests ? Explain.

key_points: India uses international norms such as non-interference and peaceful resolution of disputes to address cross-border terrorism and Pakistani support for insurgencies.
India participates in UN peacekeeping missions and supports international institutions, which enhances its global standing and provides diplomatic leverage in protecting its interests.
key_points_hindi: भारत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानदंडों जैसे अहस्तक्षेप और शांतिपूर्ण समाधान का उपयोग सीमापार आतंकवाद से निपटने के लिए करता है।
भारत संयुक्त राष्ट्र शांति रक्षा मिशनों में भाग लेता है जिससे उसकी वैश्विक प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ती है।

questions.solution: India's security interests have been protected through international norms and institutions in two significant ways. First, India invokes international norms of non-interference and peaceful resolution of disputes to highlight Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism and separatist movements in Kashmir, thereby building diplomatic pressure against such activities. Second, India's active participation in United Nations peacekeeping operations and its engagement with multilateral institutions enhances its global credibility and allows it to shape international norms that safeguard its strategic interests.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत ने अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानदंडों और संस्थाओं के माध्यम से अपनी सुरक्षा की रक्षा दो प्रकार से की है। पहला, अहस्तक्षेप के अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानदंडों का उपयोग करते हुए पाकिस्तान की सीमापार आतंकवाद की नीति को उजागर किया। दूसरा, संयुक्त राष्ट्र शांति रक्षा में भाग लेकर वैश्विक विश्वसनीयता बढ़ाई।

questions.text: केंद्र में गठबंधन सरकार के किन्हीं दो लाभों का आकलन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Assess any two advantages of coalition governments at the Centre.

key_points: Coalition governments ensure greater representation of diverse regional and social interests at the national level.
They promote a culture of consensus and compromise in policy-making, preventing dominance by a single party.
key_points_hindi: गठबंधन सरकारें विभिन्न क्षेत्रीय और सामाजिक हितों का राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर बेहतर प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित करती हैं।
वे नीति-निर्माण में सहमति और समझौते की संस्कृति को बढ़ावा देती हैं।

questions.solution: Coalition governments at the Centre offer two important advantages. First, they ensure better representation of India's diverse regional, linguistic, and social groups in the central government. Smaller regional parties that join the coalition bring the concerns of their respective states to national policy discussions, making governance more inclusive. Second, coalition governments promote political consensus and moderation. Since no single party can push through extreme or unilateral policies without the support of coalition partners, policies tend to be more balanced and broadly acceptable.
questions.solution_hindi: केंद्र में गठबंधन सरकार के दो लाभ हैं। पहला, यह भारत के विविध क्षेत्रीय, भाषाई और सामाजिक समूहों का बेहतर प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित करती है। दूसरा, गठबंधन सरकार राजनीतिक सहमति को बढ़ावा देती है और कोई एकल पार्टी अपनी चरम नीतियाँ लागू नहीं कर सकती।

questions.text: 1971 में बांग्लादेश युद्ध की ओर ले जाने वाली परिस्थितियों का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Describe the circumstances that led to the Bangladesh War in 1971.

key_points: In the 1970 elections, the Awami League under Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won a majority but was denied power by the military establishment.
The Pakistani military under Yahya Khan launched a brutal crackdown called Operation Searchlight in East Pakistan in March 1971.
Millions of East Pakistani refugees fled to India, creating a massive humanitarian and economic burden.
India intervened militarily in December 1971 to support the Bengali liberation movement, leading to the creation of Bangladesh.

questions.solution: The Bangladesh War of 1971 resulted from a series of political and military circumstances. In the 1970 general elections, the Awami League led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won a landslide majority in East Pakistan, enough to form the national government. However, the military regime of General Yahya Khan and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto of the Pakistan Peoples Party refused to transfer power, as they feared East Pakistan's political dominance. In March 1971, the Pakistani military launched Operation Searchlight — a brutal crackdown on civilians and Awami League supporters in East Pakistan. Widespread atrocities led to nearly one crore refugees fleeing into India, creating an enormous humanitarian crisis. India supported the Mukti Bahini freedom fighters, and in December 1971, the Indian Army intervened directly. After a swift military campaign, Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971, leading to the creation of the independent nation of Bangladesh.
questions.solution_hindi: 1971 का बांग्लादेश युद्ध कई राजनीतिक और सैन्य परिस्थितियों का परिणाम था। 1970 के चुनावों में अवामी लीग को बहुमत मिला लेकिन सत्ता हस्तांतरण से मना किया गया। मार्च 1971 में पाकिस्तानी सेना ने ऑपरेशन सर्चलाइट चलाया। लगभग एक करोड़ शरणार्थी भारत आए। भारत ने मुक्ति बाहिनी का समर्थन किया और दिसंबर 1971 में प्रत्यक्ष सैन्य हस्तक्षेप किया, जिससे बांग्लादेश का जन्म हुआ।

questions.text: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के कोई दो कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two reasons for the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Economic stagnation and the failure of the Soviet command economy to meet consumer needs created widespread public discontent.
The rise of nationalist and secessionist movements in Soviet republics, fuelled by the policies of glasnost and perestroika, weakened central authority.

questions.solution: The disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991 can be attributed to two major reasons. First, the Soviet economy suffered from severe structural weaknesses. The centralised command economy failed to produce consumer goods efficiently, led to technological stagnation, and could not sustain the enormous defence expenditure of the Cold War arms race. The general population experienced a declining standard of living, which eroded public faith in the communist system. Second, Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms of glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) inadvertently unleashed nationalist aspirations across Soviet republics. Baltic states, Ukraine, Georgia, and Central Asian republics began asserting their national identities and demanding independence. These movements grew too powerful for the central government to contain, and one by one, republics declared sovereignty, leading to the formal dissolution of the USSR in December 1991.
questions.solution_hindi: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के दो प्रमुख कारण थे। पहला, सोवियत केंद्रीकृत अर्थव्यवस्था उपभोक्ता वस्तुएँ कुशलतापूर्वक उत्पादित करने में विफल रही और शस्त्र प्रतिस्पर्धा का बोझ उठाने में असमर्थ हो गई। दूसरा, ग्लासनोस्त और पेरेस्त्रोइका की नीतियों ने सोवियत गणराज्यों में राष्ट्रवादी आकांक्षाओं को जन्म दिया जो केंद्र के नियंत्रण से बाहर हो गईं।

sub_questions.solution: Two effective measures to improve Indo-Pakistan relations would be as follows. key_points: Resolving the boundary dispute through sustained diplomatic negotiations and maintaining the Line of Actual Control as a zone of peace.

sub_questions.solution: Two measures to improve Indo-China relations would be the following. First, both countries should engage in sustained diplomatic negotiations to peacefully resolve the long-standing boundary dispute along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). Confidence-building measures such as border patrols protocols, hotlines between military commanders, and reaffirmation of agreements like the 1993 and 1996 border peace accords can reduce the risk of armed confrontations. The liberalisation of trade and investment policies by national governments and international institutions like the WTO has opened up markets across the world.

sub_questions.solution: Globalisation has been driven by two main causes. The internet has enabled businesses to operate seamlessly across continents, while cheaper air travel has facilitated the movement of people and ideas. questions.text_english: The best way to respond to regional aspirations is through democratic negotiations rather than through suppression. Justify the statement with examples.

key_points: Democratic negotiation and accommodation of regional aspirations leads to lasting peace, as demonstrated by the Punjab Accord and Mizoram Peace Accord.
Suppression of regional movements tends to fuel greater resentment and prolonged conflict, as initially seen in Nagaland and Punjab before negotiated settlements were reached.

questions.solution: The statement that democratic negotiations are the best way to address regional aspirations is well justified by Indian experience. When the government engaged in constructive dialogue with regional movements, lasting peace was achieved. The Mizoram Peace Accord of 1986 is an excellent example — after years of insurgency, the Indian government negotiated with the Mizo National Front, granted statehood to Mizoram, and allowed former rebels to participate in elections, successfully ending the conflict. Similarly, the Punjab Accord of 1985 attempted to address the grievances of the Akali Dal through dialogue. In contrast, wherever regional aspirations were suppressed through force alone without political accommodation, movements tended to become more radical. The Assam Agitation was ultimately resolved through the Assam Accord of 1985, which gave a constitutional and legal framework to address the concerns of the local population. These examples confirm that democratic accommodation, rather than suppression, creates durable political solutions.

options.A: वे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र के अनुकूल प्रौद्योगिकी विकसित करने में अग्रणी थे।

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). As the passage itself states, the per capita emission rates of developing countries are a tiny fraction of those in the developed world. The Kyoto Protocol exempted developing countries from binding emission reduction targets because their cumulative and per capita contributions to greenhouse gas emissions were minimal compared to industrialised nations that had been emitting since the Industrial Revolution.

sub_questions.text_english: Where was the Earth Summit held ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B): Rio de Janeiro. The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), popularly known as the Earth Summit, was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in June 1992. sub_questions.solution: India's claim to permanent membership in the UN Security Council rests on several strong grounds. First, India is the world's most populous democracy with over 1.4 billion people and one of the fastest growing major economies. As a country that represents about one-sixth of humanity, it deserves a permanent voice in the apex body responsible for international peace and security. Second, India has been one of the largest and most consistent contributors to UN peacekeeping operations since their inception, sending tens of thousands of troops across conflict zones from Africa to Southeast Asia. This demonstrates India's commitment to multilateralism and international security. Third, India is a responsible nuclear weapons state that has maintained a no-first-use policy and has consistently advocated for global disarmament. This responsible conduct reinforces its credentials as a trustworthy permanent member. Fourth, the current permanent membership of the UNSC — the P5 — reflects the power configuration of 1945 and does not represent the realities of the 21st century. Asia, the most populous and economically dynamic continent, deserves adequate permanent representation, and India is the most natural candidate from the region.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the three main complaints reflected in the resolution adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1992 to reform the UN Security Council.

key_points: The UNSC's membership is unrepresentative, as it reflects the power configuration of 1945 and excludes major modern powers from permanent membership.
The veto power of the five permanent members is undemocratic and allows a single P5 nation to block resolutions that enjoy widespread international support.
The working methods of the UNSC are opaque and lack transparency, with key decisions made in informal consultations rather than open debates.

sub_questions.solution: The 1992 UN General Assembly resolution on UNSC reform highlighted three major complaints. The first complaint was about unrepresentativeness. The Security Council's permanent membership consists of only five states — USA, UK, France, Russia, and China — chosen on the basis of their power in 1945. This outdated composition fails to reflect the emergence of new economic and political powers in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Countries like India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan, which are major contributors to the UN and to global governance, are excluded from permanent membership. The second complaint concerned the undemocratic nature of the veto. Each of the five permanent members holds veto power, allowing a single country to block any substantive UNSC resolution regardless of how many member states support it. This has repeatedly paralysed the Council on issues like the Syria conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war, undermining collective security. The third complaint related to lack of transparency. The Council's real decisions are made in informal and closed-door consultations among the P5, with formal meetings serving largely as rubber-stamping exercises. Developing countries and non-permanent members feel excluded from meaningful participation, making the Council unaccountable to the broader UN membership.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe the difficulties faced by India to get the merger of all the Princely States into the Union of India.

key_points: The Princely States had treaty rights with the British Crown that lapsed on independence, leaving them technically free to remain independent or join either India or Pakistan.
Some rulers like the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Nawab of Junagadh refused to accede to India, necessitating firm political and military action.

sub_questions.solution: India faced enormous difficulties in integrating the Princely States into the Union after independence. At the time of British withdrawal in August 1947, there were 565 Princely States that had treaty relationships with the British Crown. These treaties lapsed with independence, leaving the states technically free to decide their own future. The first major difficulty was that some rulers harboured ambitions of independence. The Nizam of Hyderabad, the Nawab of Junagadh, and the Maharaja of Travancore initially refused to accede to India. The Nizam even sought UN intervention and maintained his own army. The second difficulty arose from the geographic position of states like Hyderabad and Junagadh, which were surrounded by Indian territory but whose rulers wanted to remain independent or join Pakistan. This created administrative and security complications. Third, some rulers exploited the confusion of the transition period to delay integration, hoping for more favourable terms or for international developments to support their independence. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon managed this enormous challenge through a combination of persuasion, guarantees of privy purses, and when necessary, police action and military force, successfully completing the integration of nearly all states by 1950.

sub_questions.text: हैदराबाद रियासत को भारतीय संघ में विलय की ओर ले जाने वाले घटनाक्रम का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the events that led to the accession of Hyderabad into the Union of India.

key_points: The Nizam of Hyderabad refused to accede to India at the time of independence and declared Hyderabad's independence.
The Nizam encouraged the Razakars, a paramilitary force, who terrorised the local Hindu population and destabilised the region.
After months of negotiations failed, India launched 'Operation Polo' (Police Action) in September 1948.
Within five days, the Indian Army overran Hyderabad and the Nizam surrendered, leading to Hyderabad's accession to India.

sub_questions.solution: The accession of Hyderabad into the Indian Union was a dramatic chain of events. When India became independent in August 1947, the Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, refused to accede to India. Hyderabad, though surrounded entirely by Indian territory, was the largest and wealthiest Princely State. The Nizam declared Hyderabad an independent state and even approached the United Nations, seeking international recognition of his sovereignty. He also signed a standstill agreement with India to buy time, while attempting to purchase arms abroad. Within Hyderabad, the Nizam encouraged a fanatical paramilitary organisation called the Razakars, led by Qasim Razvi, which committed widespread atrocities against the majority Hindu population and anyone who favoured accession to India. The Razakars also began crossing into Indian territory and attacking villages. After months of patient diplomacy failed to move the Nizam, Sardar Patel ordered the Indian Army to act. In September 1948, India launched 'Operation Polo', officially called a Police Action. Within five days, the Indian Army defeated Hyderabad's forces. On 17 September 1948, the Nizam surrendered and signed the instrument of accession, and Hyderabad became part of the Indian Union.

sub_questions.solution: Four major developments in Indian politics since 1989 are as follows. First, the 1989 general elections marked the end of the Congress Party's era of single-party dominance that had lasted since independence. The National Front government under V.P. Singh came to power, inaugurating the era of coalition politics where no single party would command an outright majority in Parliament for the next two decades. Second, the implementation of the Mandal Commission Report in 1990, providing 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes in central government jobs, was a watershed event. It fundamentally altered the social basis of Indian politics, empowering lower-caste groups but also triggering upper-caste protests and reshaping political alliances. Third, the demolition of the Babri Masjid in December 1992 and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement led to a dramatic rise in the electoral fortunes of the Bharatiya Janata Party. By 1996 and 1998, the BJP emerged as India's single largest party, eventually forming stable governments under Atal Bihari Vajpayee from 1999 to 2004. Fourth, the economic liberalisation reforms launched in 1991 under Prime Minister Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh dismantled the licence-permit raj, opened the economy to foreign investment, and set India on a path of sustained high economic growth, fundamentally altering the relationship between the state and the market.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three issues on which a general consensus has emerged among most of the political parties of India.

key_points: Economic liberalisation and the shift to a market economy is broadly accepted across parties, with disagreements only on pace and extent.
A consensus exists on the importance of caste-based reservations for SCs, STs and OBCs in education and government jobs.
All major parties broadly accept the importance of federalism and the need to respect the autonomy of state governments.

sub_questions.solution: Three issues on which a broad consensus has emerged among most Indian political parties are as follows. First, there is a near-universal consensus on the broad direction of economic policy — namely, economic liberalisation and the promotion of a market economy. While parties may disagree on the pace and extent of privatisation or on social welfare spending, no major political party today advocates returning to the old socialist command economy model of the pre-1991 era. All parties accept that India's integration into the global economy has been beneficial. Second, all major political parties have come to accept the policy of affirmative action and reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes in education and government employment. This was once contested, but the political arithmetic of India's diverse electorate means that no party can afford to oppose reservations. Third, there is a broad consensus on the importance of respecting the federal structure and the autonomy of state governments. Whether ruling at the Centre or in opposition, parties that come from regional bases have consistently demanded that states be given greater financial and administrative powers. The National Development Council, Finance Commission recommendations, and inter-state council mechanisms enjoy broad cross-party support.
